scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Hardness of finding large independent sets in three-colorable graphs” (preprints/Hardness-of-finding-large-independent-sets-in-three-colorable-graphs-September-24-2026/Hardness-of-finding-large-independent-sets-in-three-colorable-graphs-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 106 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ae304fee9351517), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed real 0 < δ < 1/3, there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm Rδ that maps each explicitly encoded Boolean 3-CNF formula ϕ to a nonempty finite simple undirected unweighted graph Gϕ such that ϕ is satisfiable =⇒ Gϕ is three-colorable, ϕ is unsatisfiable =⇒ α(Gϕ) < δ |V (Gϕ)|. The running time and explicit output size are polynomial in the ordinary binary encoding length of ϕ. Their constants and polynomial degree may depend on the fixed δ, but not on ϕ. The coloring in the first implication covers every vertex and is not supplied with the graph.
